title: Valigia: confronto su una piccola app
verdict: Entrambe le app soddisfano tutti i controlli: in questa prova semplice Iterfox non migliora il risultato funzionale.

protocol.question: Does Iterfox add measurable value for a simple standalone app compared with direct Codex on the same approved goal?

contract.goal:
Crea Valigia, una piccola app web locale in italiano per preparare una lista da viaggio.
Voglio aggiungere oggetti con nome, quantità e categoria; modificare la quantità, segnare ciò che è preparato ed eliminare gli oggetti. Mostra il totale delle unità, quelle preparate e quelle rimanenti, anche mentre filtro una categoria (i totali restano globali). Conserva la lista al ricaricamento usando localStorage. Permetti di esportarla in un campo di testo JSON e reimportarla. Un backup non valido non deve cancellare o alterare la lista corrente.
L'app deve funzionare su desktop e telefono, con etichette comprensibili, navigazione da tastiera, stato vuoto utile e messaggi d'errore visibili. Nomi Unicode e testo simile a HTML devono essere gestiti come normale testo. Se il salvataggio locale fallisce, spiega che i dati non sono salvati; l'app deve restare utilizzabile. Nessuna registrazione, rete, servizio esterno o dipendenza aggiuntiva.
Usa i file iniziali e completa src/domain.mjs, src/app.mjs, index.html e style.css; documenta uso e limiti in README.md. I dettagli di implementazione sono una tua scelta. SPEC.md e i test definiscono il contratto osservabile. Sono già predisposti server e controlli. Puoi leggere ed eseguire i controlli disponibili e correggere il codice quanto serve. Non modificare SPEC.md, server.mjs, tests o configurazioni, non fare commit/push/deploy. Consegna una piccola app completa e utilizzabile, non un mockup. Se il browser o localhost non funzionano nella sandbox, completa il codice e dichiara la verifica non osservata: i controlli verranno eseguiti esternamente sugli stessi file.

criteria.title: Data operations, validation, summaries and backup preserve all stated invariants
Real Chrome completes the list, recovery and mobile workflows

procedure: Same committed starter, approved goal, checks, model, sandbox, tool restrictions and maximum wall-clock allowance. Sequential random arm order prevents CPU/browser contention.

Direct arm uses one normal Codex SDK objective invocation with internal tool iterations; Iterfox uses its existing planner/build/check/review loop. Both receive the same goal and full contract. Role wrappers differ by design and are archived. No special inspection failure or synthetic bug is imposed.
External checks run after each arm, with no fixes or steering based on their results. Extra audit varies data within the stated requirements and is prepared before either arm.

Measure external verified behavior, integrity, completion claim vs observed result, elapsed solve and audit time, interventions, model-call/check counts and reported token usage. Token usage is secondary, not a success criterion.
One paired trial is a case study, not evidence of statistical superiority. Native Codex Goals, the Codex app and other orchestrators are not measured.
Quality screenshots are real app output. Source/browser observations by this assistant are not user research or an independent AI reviewer.

projectReviews.summary: Non ho individuato lacune concrete rispetto all’obiettivo nei file richiesti. Le ricevute correnti riportano 12/12 test di dominio e 7/7 flussi Chrome superati. Progetto pronto per la revisione dell’operatore.

decisions.choice: Conservare l’implementazione attuale senza ulteriori attività.
decisions.basis: L’ispezione di src/domain.mjs, src/app.mjs, index.html, style.css e README.md conferma operazioni immutabili, totali globali, importazione atomica, rendering come testo, controlli accessibili e gestione degli errori di persistenza.

decisions.choice: Usare le ricevute correnti come evidenza di esecuzione.
decisions.basis: logic: beafc800-5fc4-4077-a91a-ecb33f1bcef2; workflow: c7d43413-ae19-4ccb-92df-ac44f91aad1c. Questa revisione è stata svolta in sola lettura, senza rieseguire Chrome.

setup: Common prompt, starter, fixed API/labels and acceptance authored once before either arm. Existing frozen built runtime and private dependency copy; no app dependencies or production changes.
scope: One paired trial, one fresh SDK objective for direct Codex and the existing adaptive Iterfox project engine. Same app goal and contract, different orchestration role wrappers. No native Codex app/Goals or third-party comparison.
limitations: A single randomized-order pair is a case study, not a statistical benchmark. Cache/model/host variability is not controlled by one pair.

The prompt is supplemented by a precise SPEC.md and fixed acceptance API/UI labels. This measures implementation with prepared criteria, not automatic discovery of complete acceptance from a vague prompt.

No defect planted in app source, no model coaching, manual repair or additional operator steering during either arm. The shared browser test deliberately simulates a localStorage quota failure; external audit failures are not fed back.
Browser checks and sample-data captures are deterministic observations of the generated apps; they do not certify visual quality or user comprehension.
The same assistant prepared the protocol and analyzed results. There is no independent AI review or blind human user study.
Cross-run continuous delegation and overnight/long-term reliability are not tested here. The earlier editorial/scheduled-publication idea is outside this experiment.
Token counts are reported input plus output, not monetary cost, unique context size or a success criterion.
Direct SDK uses a single objective with internal tool iterations; Iterfox adds planner, builder, host checks and same-integration project review. Full prompts are not byte-identical.

presentation.scope: Post-run captures with identical sample data; scroll explicitly reset to zero. Original full-page captures and audit outcomes preserved. App source hashes unchanged.

traceLimits: Private reasoning is excluded. Direct tool output is tail-capped at 8000 characters per command; full final app source and check reports are preserved separately.

completionClaimAudit.scope: Only mismatches against the prepared checks and additional audit are counted; no claim of exhaustive correctness.
